ei.title: Questioning That Hard Work Is Best
ei.subject: 11월_2022 고1 모의고사
ei.lesson: Questioning That Hard Work Is Best

fullPassage: Our language helps to reveal our deeper assumptions. Think of these revealing phrases: When we accomplish something important, we say it took "blood, sweat, and tears." We say important achievements are "hard-earned." We recommend a "hard day's work" when "day's work" would be enough. When we talk of "easy money," we are implying it was obtained through illegal or questionable means. We use the phrase "That's easy for you to say" as a criticism, usually when we are seeking to invalidate someone's opinion. It's like we all automatically accept that the "right" way is, inevitably, the harder one. In my experience this is hardly ever questioned. What would happen if you do challenge this sacred cow? We don't even pause to consider that something important and valuable could be made easy. What if the biggest thing keeping us from doing what matters is the false assumption that it has to take huge effort?

questions.passage: Our language helps to (A)[conceal / reveal] our deeper assumptions. Think of these revealing phrases: When we accomplish something important, we say it took "blood, sweat, and tears." We say important achievements are "hard-earned." We recommend a "hard day's work" when "day's work" would be enough. When we talk of "easy money," we are implying it was obtained through (B)[illegal / legal] or questionable means. It's like we all automatically accept that the "right" way is, inevitably, the harder one. In my experience this is hardly ever questioned. What would happen if you do challenge this sacred cow? We don't even pause to consider that something important and valuable could be made easy. What if the biggest thing keeping us from doing what matters is the (C)[true / false] assumption that it has to take huge effort?
questions.stem: 다음 글의 (A), (B), (C)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것끼리 짝지은 것은?

det.analysis:
① conceal: 언어가 우리의 가정을 '드러낸다(reveal)'는 흐름이므로 conceal(숨기다)은 부적절
② reveal — illegal — false ←정답
③ legal: 'easy money(쉬운 돈)'는 '불법적(illegal)'이거나 의심스러운 수단을 암시하므로 legal(합법의)은 부적절
④ true: 마지막 문장은 노력이 필요하다는 것이 '잘못된(false)' 가정이라고 하므로 true는 부적절
det.tip: 언어가 가정을 드러내는지, easy money가 어떤 수단을 암시하는지, 마지막 가정의 성격을 파악하세요.

det.korean: (A) 비판/칭찬 (B) 더 힘든/더 쉬운 (C) 가치 있는/가치 없는
det.analysis:
① compliment: '그건 너한테나 쉬운 말이지'는 상대 의견을 무효화하려는 '비판(criticism)'이므로 compliment(칭찬)는 부적절
② easier: 옳은 방식은 필연적으로 '더 힘든(harder)' 것이라고 받아들인다고 했으므로 easier는 부적절
③ criticism — harder — valuable ←정답
④ worthless: 중요하고 '가치 있는(valuable)' 것이라고 했으므로 worthless는 부적절
det.tip: That's easy for you to say의 어감, right way의 성격, important and __의 문맥을 파악하세요.

det.tip: challenge는 동사로 '이의를 제기하다', 명사로 '어려운 과제'라는 뜻이 있습니다. 문맥으로 구분하세요.

④ questionable ←정답: '정직하거나 합법적이거나 사실이 아닐 가능성이 있는; 의심을 일으키는'
det.tip: 'causing doubt(의심을 일으키는)'에 주목하세요.

questions.passage: When we talk of "easy money," we are __________ (imply) it was obtained through illegal or questionable means. We use the phrase "That's easy for you to say" as a criticism.
questions.stem:
다음 글의 빈칸에 괄호 안의 단어를 알맞은 형태로 바꿔

(imply) 영어로 쓰시오. (1단어)

det.korean: '쉬운 돈'을 말할 때, 우리는 그것이 불법적이거나 의심스러운 수단으로 얻어졌음을 암시하고 있다.
det.analysis: 진행형 전환: 'we are __________'에서 be동사(are) 뒤에는 동사원형이 올 수 없고 현재분사(-ing)가 와야 하므로 imply를 implying으로 바꾼다. 'be동사 + -ing'는 '~하고 있다'는 진행의 뜻이다.
det.tip: be동사(are) 뒤 동사는 -ing 형태(현재분사)로 씁니다: are implying.

questions.passage: It's like we all automatically accept that the "right" way is, inevitably, the harder one. In my experience this is hardly ever __________ (question).
questions.stem:
다음 글의 빈칸에 괄호 안의 단어를 알맞은 형태로 바꿔

(question) 영어로 쓰시오. (1단어)

det.korean: 우리는 모두 옳은 방식이 필연적으로 더 힘든 것이라고 자동으로 받아들이는 것 같다. 내 경험상 이것은 좀처럼 의문시되지 않는다.
det.analysis: 수동태 전환: 주어 this(=이 생각)는 '의문을 제기하는' 주체가 아니라 '의문시되는' 대상이므로 'be동사(is) + 과거분사'의 수동태가 필요하다. 따라서 question을 questioned로 바꾼다.
det.tip: '~되다'라는 수동의 뜻이면 be동사 + 과거분사(-ed): is questioned.

questions.passage: Our language helps to reveal our deeper assumptions. Think of these revealing phrases: When we accomplish something important, we say it took "blood, sweat, and tears." We say important achievements are "hard-earned." We recommend a "hard day's work" when "day's work" would be enough. When we talk of "easy money," we are implying it was obtained through illegal or questionable means. We use the phrase "That's easy for you to say" as a criticism, usually when we are seeking to invalidate someone's opinion. It's like we all automatically accept that the "right" way is, inevitably, __________. In my experience this is hardly ever questioned. What would happen if you do challenge this sacred cow? We don't even pause to consider that something important and valuable could be made easy. What if the biggest thing keeping us from doing what matters is the false assumption that it has to take huge effort?
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: 더 힘든 것 / 더 빠른 방식 / 유일한 선택 / 잘못된 길
det.analysis:
① the harder one ←정답: 글 전체가 '옳은 방식 = 더 힘든 방식'이라는 가정을 다루므로 적절
② the faster way: 속도는 문맥과 무관
③ the only choice: 유일한 선택은 언급되지 않음
④ the wrong path: 잘못된 길은 'right way'와 충돌
det.tip: 글 전체가 '옳은 것 = 힘든 것'이라는 가정을 비판한다는 점을 파악하세요.

det.korean: 적은 시간 / 막대한 노력 / 큰 행운 / 많은 돈
